hints: If the rectangle is already a square, it needs no cut.
Try a vertical first cut at every width and a horizontal first cut at every height.
Each cut splits the job into two smaller rectangles, whose minimum cut counts can be added.
analogy: Try each possible first guillotine cut and keep the one that leaves the least work in both pieces.
example: A 3x5 rectangle can be cut into a 3x3 square and 3x2 rectangle; then split 3x2 into squares, for 3 cuts total.
algorithm: For all dimensions up to the target, set dp[a][b]=0 when a=b; otherwise minimize 1+dp[left]+dp[right] over all vertical and horizontal splits.
correctness: Any valid cutting plan has a first cut; after it, its two independent pieces must each be solved optimally, so considering all first cuts finds the optimum.
complexity: O(a*b*(a+b)) time and O(ab) space for an a-by-b rectangle.
